accepted.s: Physiological density is defined as the ratio of:
o: Agricultural population to total geographical area
Total population to net cultivated area
Total population to total geographical area
Agricultural population to net cultivated area
accepted.x: Physiological density is total population divided by net cultivated area. Agricultural density uses agricultural population divided by net cultivable area.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related density concepts by identifying the correct denominator.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding population density according to Census 2011:

List-I (Unit)
 a. Bihar
 b. West Bengal
 c. Kerala
 d. Arunachal Pradesh

List-II (Persons per square kilometre)
 i. 17
 ii. 860
 iii. 1,106
 iv. 1,028

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i
a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i
accepted.x: Bihar recorded 1,106 persons per square kilometre, West Bengal 1,028, Kerala 860 and Arunachal Pradesh 17.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong match.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following Union Territories recorded the highest population density according to Census 2011?
o: Chandigarh
Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Puducherry
NCT of Delhi
accepted.x: NCT of Delhi had the highest density among the Union Territories, at 11,320 persons per square kilometre.
accepted.tq: Use the highest-value comparison within a specified category.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Puducherry — 2,598 persons per sq km
Chandigarh — 9,258 persons per sq km
Andaman and Nicobar Islands — 46 persons per sq km
Mizoram — 86 persons per sq km
accepted.x: Mizoram had a density of 52 persons per square kilometre. Sikkim, not Mizoram, had a density of 86.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly matched numerical pair by comparing adjacent values in the density sequence.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following units in ascending order of population density according to Census 2011:
A. Sikkim
B. Arunachal Pradesh
C. Mizoram
D. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
o: B, D, C, A
D, B, C, A
B, C, D, A
A, C, D, B
accepted.x: The ascending order is Arunachal Pradesh (17), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (46), Mizoram (52) and Sikkim (86).
accepted.tq: Arrange numerical values from the lowest to the highest.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the population-density order among the southern States, from highest to lowest, according to the figures provided?
o: Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh
Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The order is Kerala (860), Tamil Nadu (555), Karnataka (319) and residual Andhra Pradesh (304).
accepted.tq: Compare all entries in the same regional group before selecting the complete order.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: With reference to the population density of the old 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct?
o: Prakasam had the highest density, while Krishna had a density below 200.
Krishna had the highest density, while YSR Kadapa and Prakasam had densities below 200.
YSR Kadapa had the highest density, while Krishna had the lowest density.
All the three districts had densities above 500.
accepted.x: Krishna had the highest density at 518, whereas YSR Kadapa and Prakasam had densities below 200.
accepted.tq: Test the highest-and-lowest comparison within a local administrative region.
accepted.sec: Population density - definition, trend, highest/lowest states and UTs, South India, AP  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the least populous units listed in the material, beginning with the least populous?
o: Lakshadweep, Sikkim, Daman and Diu, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli
Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Sikkim, Chandigarh
Sikkim, Lakshadweep, Chandigarh, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli
Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Sikkim, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Chandigarh
accepted.x: The listed least populous units are Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Sikkim and Chandigarh, in that order.
accepted.tq: Identify the specified least-populous sequence rather than confusing States with Union Territories.
accepted.sec: Distribution of population - most/least populous states, BIMARU  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The term ‘BIMARU’ refers to which of the following groups of States?
o: Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and West Bengal
Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh
Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: BIMARU is formed from Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test an acronym by expanding each component without substituting a neighbouring State.
accepted.sec: Distribution of population - most/least populous states, BIMARU  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who coined the term ‘BIMARU’ in the mid-1980s?
o: Ashish Bose
Meadows
Registrar General of India
United Nations Population Division
accepted.x: The term BIMARU was coined by demographer Ashish Bose in the mid-1980s.
accepted.tq: Match a distinctive term with its associated scholar rather than its later institutional users.
accepted.sec: Distribution of population - most/least populous states, BIMARU  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the population-growth comparison associated with the BIMARU States?
o: Growth rates were identical in the BIMARU and southern States.
The term BIMARU refers exclusively to States with declining populations.
Growth was faster in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan than in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
Growth was faster in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh than in the BIMARU States.
accepted.x: Population growth was faster in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan than in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. This difference is associated with the delimitation dispute.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish the two regional groups.
accepted.sec: Distribution of population - most/least populous states, BIMARU  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to UN World Population Prospects 2024, India accounts for approximately what share of the world’s population?
o: 11.7 percent
15.7 percent
17.7 percent
21.7 percent
accepted.x: UN WPP 2024 places India’s share of the world population at approximately 17.7 percent.
accepted.tq: Select the precise percentage rather than the nearby altered figure.
accepted.sec: Population projections - India overtaking China, UN WPP  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the projected population figures for India mentioned in the population projections?
o: 1,363.0 million in 2021 and 1,522.3 million by 2036
1,463.0 million in 2021 and 1,522.3 million by 2036
1,363.0 million in 2021 and 1,422.3 million by 2036
1,263.0 million in 2021 and 1,522.3 million by 2036
accepted.x: India’s estimated population was 1,363.0 million in 2021 and is projected to reach 1,522.3 million by 2036.
accepted.tq: Check both the base-year estimate and the projection instead of relying on one familiar figure.
accepted.sec: Population projections - India overtaking China, UN WPP  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The projected population figure of India for 2036 was prepared by which body mentioned in the population projections?
o: Technical Group on Population Projections, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Finance Commission of India
NITI Aayog Population Census Division
United Nations Environment Programme
accepted.x: The projection of 1,522.3 million by 2036 was prepared by the Technical Group on Population Projections under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which body prepared it?’ test to distinguish the responsible institution.
accepted.sec: Population projections - India overtaking China, UN WPP  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2027:
1. It is being conducted digitally.
2. It is proposed to be the first caste census of independent India.
3. Preliminary work is underway in snow-bound areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Census 2027 is described as the first digital census and the first caste census of independent India, with preparatory work underway in snow-bound areas.
accepted.tq: Treat each current-affairs feature as an independent statement and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1872 — First census in India
1881 — First census in India
2011 — First synchronous census in India
2027 — Last census held in India
accepted.x: The first census was held in 1872. The first synchronous census was held in 1881, while 2011 was the last census held before Census 2027.
accepted.tq: Separate the first census, first synchronous census and last completed census by their dates.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the historical census sequence is correct?
o: The only decline in population occurred during 2001–11, and 2027 was the first synchronous census.
The only decline in population occurred during 1951–61, and 2011 was the first synchronous census.
The only decline in population occurred during 1911–21, and 1881 was the first synchronous census.
The only decline in population occurred during 1881–91, and 1872 was the first synchronous census.
accepted.x: The only population decline occurred during 1911–21. The first synchronous census was conducted in 1881.
accepted.tq: Combine two chronology facts and reject options that swap the event and date.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the population-growth and density comparison of Andhra Pradesh with India during 2001–2011?
o: Andhra Pradesh recorded 17.70 percent growth and a density of 304, compared with India’s 9.21 percent growth and density of 382.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.21 percent growth and a density of 382, compared with India’s 17.70 percent growth and density of 304.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.21 percent growth and a density of 304, compared with India’s 17.70 percent growth and density of 382.
Andhra Pradesh recorded 21.13 percent growth and a density of 382, both higher than India.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.21 percent growth and a density of 304, approximately half and below India’s corresponding figures of 17.70 percent and 382.
accepted.tq: Compare two regions across two indicators and watch for reversed figures.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s population growth rate fell from which figure to which figure, leading to the reported policy discussion on encouraging a third child?
o: 9.21 percent to 7.00 percent
21.13 percent to 9.21 percent
17.70 percent to 9.21 percent
21.13 percent to 17.70 percent
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s growth rate declined from 21.13 percent to 9.21 percent. The State subsequently offered incentives connected with having a third child.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of change correctly and distinguish State figures from the national figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as a major concern of southern States regarding delimitation after Census 2027?
o: Their geographical area may be reduced by constitutional amendment.
Their share of seats may decline because they controlled population growth more effectively.
Their density figures may be excluded from the Census.
They may lose all representation in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.x: Southern States, including Andhra Pradesh, fear a reduction in their seat share because delimitation based on population may disadvantage States that controlled population growth.
accepted.tq: Apply the demographic trend to its constitutional and political consequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following concerns has been raised by former officials regarding the population-enumeration process?
o: Possible links between NPR and NRC through the collection of parents’ details
Exclusion of all urban households from the enumeration
Abolition of the Registrar General’s office
Replacement of the Census by a purely agricultural survey
accepted.x: Former officials have expressed concern that details of parents may create possible links between the National Population Register and the National Register of Citizens.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional relationship in a criticism-based question.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Census Town classification is correct?
o: The Census Town definition was first introduced in 2011 and is being abolished in 2027.
The Census Town definition is determined by the World Population Prospects.
The 1981 definition applies only to rural villages and not to towns.
The Registrar General of India is retaining the 1981 Census Town definition.
accepted.x: The Registrar General of India is retaining the Census Town definition formulated in 1981.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-and-year combination to reject institution and definition swaps.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current stage of Census 2027 mentioned in the material?
o: The House Listing Operation was conducted from January to March 2024.
The population enumeration was completed in 2011 and no preparatory work is underway.
The House Listing Operation was conducted from April to September 2026.
The House Listing Operation began only after the completion of Census 2027.
accepted.x: The Census 2027 House Listing Operation was conducted during April–September 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a preparatory census operation from the final population enumeration.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
